To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the 4D haptic probe is the best tool for exploring 4D topologies in 3D, (ii) the 4th Dimensional audio tag is an essential tool for understanding 4D topographies in 3D and (iii) the 4-Dimensional cutaway is a necessary tool for understanding 3D projections of 4D topography.

(1) haptic exploration of the fourth spatial dimension is possible, and can provide a more accurate representation than the visual projection of a 4D shape; (2) haptic feedback can be enhanced using audio and visual cues; and (3) dynamic tactile exploration of 4D shapes is possible and can provide a richer experience than static exploration.
the use of multimodal feedback, especially haptic feedback, in conjunction with a carefully designed 4D visualization paradigm, can provide a powerful tool for exploring the fourth dimension.

the design and evaluation of a multimodal paradigm that exploits the full richness of 4D topologies, as well as with the development of new methods for 4D visualization that are based on the use of 3D haptic and 3D graphics.
the development of a new paradigm for exploring topologically complex 4D objects.
exploring the full potential of multimodal feedback in 3D and 4D visualization.
